home.headline: Silicon for motion, power and sensing.
home.context: Explore DeepGrid product architectures, their role in your equipment, and the evidence needed before adoption. Review funding milestones and partnership opportunities.
home.decision: The investment brief lists what ₹10 Cr buys and what each chip has proven.

products.headline: Eleven mature-node chips and one drone SoC, from a 120 V motor controller to a 77 GHz radar.
products.context: Eleven mature-node products and the separate D100 programme address different equipment needs. Compare the function, what it could replace and what remains to be proven before adoption.
products.decision: Shortlist a part, then agree the evidence needed to adopt it.

technology.headline: DG32 control and hardware safety.
technology.context: Two RISC-V cores run two cycles apart. A comparator checks every committed store, latches the first cause and drives FAULT_N, which can switch off the motor bridge without waiting for firmware: 39 cycles in simulation.
technology.decision: The 39-cycle fault response is simulated; the evidence register shows what is measured.

safety.headline: DG32 drives FAULT_N 39 cycles after a lockstep mismatch, in simulation, without firmware.
safety.context: DG32’s fault path is designed to act without waiting for application software. For a buyer, the key question is whether the complete machine reaches its intended safe state under the failures that matter.
safety.decision: DG32’s response ends at the FAULT_N pin; the machine’s safe state is proven on the customer’s bench.

control.headline: The CPU runs two regulators, not the loop.
control.context: A predictable control workload can leave capacity for diagnostics. That capacity depends on operating speed, signal quality and the work the product must perform.
control.decision: About 300 hardware cycles per current loop leave a fixed budget for diagnostics.

die.headline: DG32 functional blocks and safety boundaries.
die.context: The design groups control, memory, sensing and communications around a defined safety core. Use the layout to understand which functions can change and which constraints remain fixed.
die.decision: Peripherals change per customer; the lockstep core and fault path stay fixed.

package.headline: 44 signals in a 9 × 9 mm package.
package.context: The package, interfaces and supply requirements set the integration work for the equipment maker. Some choices are defined today; final electrical limits depend on silicon characterisation.
package.decision: Pinout and package are fixed now; electrical limits wait for first-silicon characterisation.

applications.headline: Twelve architectures. Five system roles.
applications.context: DeepGrid’s portfolio by the systems it goes into. Open a chip for what it replaces and its SKU Blueprint page; DG32-LITE, the pre-silicon proof point, opens into its diagnostic story: thirty tasks that fit its one core, and the sensor that limits them.
applications.decision: Each application maps a failure mode to the chip that catches it.

uc-motors.headline: SKU-1 runs the motor; DG32-LITE can switch its bridge off without firmware.
uc-motors.context: The motor controller and safety supervisor address different responsibilities. Assess both against the drive, its operating conditions and the consequences of failure.
uc-motors.decision: SKU-1 closes the current loop in under 1 µs on motor supplies up to 120 V.

uc-vehicles.headline: Three chips for the vehicle zone: the SKU-9 gateway, the SKU-7 radar and DG32-LITE.
uc-vehicles.context: DeepGrid’s proposed parts serve sensing, displays, power and communications around the vehicle. Their value depends on how they fit the vehicle architecture and safety responsibilities.
uc-vehicles.decision: SKU-9 switches 16 smart fuses and eight CAN-FD buses inside one zone.

uc-defence.headline: Three parts for screened platforms: 28 V power rails, a GPS-free drone SoC and a rugged display driver.
uc-defence.context: Defence, aviation and drone programmes need both a suitable component and the evidence required for their operating environment. Country of origin does not replace performance or qualification.
uc-defence.decision: Each grade has its own screening route: MIL-STD-883, EN 50155 or radiation testing.

uc-grid.headline: SKU-2 meters to Class 0.5S and keeps the tamper record while mains is cut.
uc-grid.context: Utilities need accurate energy measurement, tamper evidence and continuity through outages. Evaluate these outcomes together before judging the proposed integration benefit.
uc-grid.decision: Class 0.5S is a design target; a utility trial against its tender is the acceptance test.

uc-boards.headline: Three board parts below the firmware: a four-rail supervisor, a secure MCU and a bus transceiver.
uc-boards.context: Power supervision and interfaces are small parts of a board with system-wide consequences. Select them against actual supply disturbances, wiring and service conditions.
uc-boards.decision: SKU-6 checks four rails with an 8 µs deglitch before it releases reset.

evidence.headline: DG32 validation is pre-silicon; qualification remains ahead.
evidence.context: Design studies, simulation, prototypes and measured silicon support different decisions. This register helps separate an opportunity worth evaluating from a product ready for deployment.
evidence.decision: No DeepGrid part has measured silicon yet; first silicon is the December 2026 shuttle.

procurement.headline: DG32 leads the STM32G0 on lockstep, DShot and CORDIC. The G0 leads on ADC and embedded flash.
procurement.context: Compare DG32’s proposed strengths with the functions, measurements and qualification your product requires. Roadmap items should remain explicit dependencies in an adoption plan.
procurement.decision: An evaluation fixes the acceptance tests, the silicon milestone and the fallback part.

resources.headline: Technical documents, decks and films.
resources.context: Start with the portfolio for product scope, the evidence register for maturity, or the detailed documents for integration. Every source has a different role in an evaluation.
resources.decision: The portfolio sets scope, the evidence register sets maturity, the documents set integration detail.

docs.headline: Nine product specifications open to read; 21 more documents on request.
docs.context: The October 2026 Blueprint defines the current portfolio. Architecture and test documents explain particular designs and results; they do not establish readiness beyond their stated scope.
docs.decision: The October 2026 SKU Blueprint is the current scope; older documents are marked superseded.

videos.headline: Ten narrated part films, plus the DG32 fault path in 1 min 26 s.
videos.context: The films explain the proposed jobs and mechanisms across the portfolio. Use them to build context, then use the source documents and evidence register for a decision.
videos.decision: The films illustrate mechanisms; measured figures live in the evidence register.

read.headline: Product requirements, operating limits and evaluation assumptions.
read.context: A source is useful when its scope, date and evidence match the decision being made. Keep design targets separate from measured results and current product status.
read.decision: Every figure here is a design value, a process nominal or an analytic estimate.

ask.headline: Ask DeepGrid
ask.context: Ask a question about DeepGrid. Read the answer, then open the supporting sources for further detail.
ask.decision: Every answer cites its sources; the evidence register shows their status.

about.headline: A semiconductor company for edge AI, in Hyderabad.
about.context: DeepGrid’s portfolio connects control, power, sensing and interfaces to physical systems. The company story explains that focus; individual product evidence determines what can be adopted.
about.decision: Each strategy claim traces to a product page and its evidence.

team.headline: 28 engineers: 10 in silicon and hardware, 7 in firmware, 6 in AI.
team.context: Leadership and advisers provide company context. A successful programme also needs clear responsibilities for product definition, validation, manufacturing and qualification.
team.decision: Fabrication, physical design, IP and boards run through named partner firms.

recognition.headline: Top 50 Startups in Telangana (2024) and TiE50 Hyderabad.
recognition.context: Awards and ecosystem participation describe the company’s development. Assess product maturity separately through the published evidence and the requirements of your programme.
recognition.decision: Awards describe the company; the evidence register describes the chips.

company.headline: One RISC-V platform and verification flow, reused across eleven mature-node chips.
company.context: The mature-node portfolio shares selected foundations while retaining product-specific development and qualification. The commercial route is through equipment makers and the systems they deliver.
company.decision: Each chip is funded against its own first-silicon milestone.

contact.headline: Request an investment discussion, a partnership or an engineering evaluation.
contact.context: Request an investment discussion, strategic partnership or engineering evaluation. Ask for the evidence and materials needed for your next decision.
contact.decision: Every reply names what is architecture, what is evidence and what needs testing.

sku1.headline: SKU-1 puts motor control and gate drive on one 130 nm BCD chip, for motor supplies up to 120 V.
sku1.context: A controller and gate driver usually require separate parts. SKU-1 proposes to combine those roles for motors, appliances and actuators.
sku1.decision: The datapath is FPGA-validated at 81.25 MHz; the 120 V power stage waits for silicon.

sku2.headline: SKU-2 meters energy to Class 0.5S and keeps the tamper record on an always-on domain under 2 µW.
sku2.context: SKU-2 brings energy measurement, meter control and outage records together for utilities and meter makers.
sku2.decision: The metrology chain is FPGA-validated; Class 0.5S accuracy is not yet measured.

sku3.headline: SKU-3 makes four sequenced rails from a 28 V bus, designed for a 100 V input spike.
sku3.context: SKU-3 targets the power supplies used in military, railway and space equipment, where qualification is part of the buying decision.
sku3.decision: The sky130 prototype tests control logic and low-voltage rails; the 28 V stage arrives on SCL 180 nm.

sku4.headline: SKU-4 runs a checker core two cycles behind and drives FAULT_N 39 cycles after a mismatch, in simulation.
sku4.context: SKU-4 uses two processors to detect disagreement and trigger a hardware fault response. It is intended to support a system safety case.
sku4.decision: 39 cycles is a simulation result, not an ISO 26262 certificate.

sku5.headline: SKU-5 carries RS-485 and 8 Mbps CAN-FD on one transceiver, with a ±15 kV pin-protection target.
sku5.context: SKU-5 targets the wired interfaces used across industrial and vehicle equipment, combining bus functions on one part.
sku5.decision: ±15 kV protection and 1.2 km RS-485 runs need tests on real wiring.

sku6.headline: SKU-6 watches four supply rails and latches a fault after an 8 µs deglitch.
sku6.context: SKU-6 watches supply conditions and records a fault so the wider system can respond. It targets a function needed across many boards.
sku6.decision: The 8 µs deglitch has to be proven against the board’s own supply noise.

sku7.headline: SKU-7 sweeps 4 GHz at 77 GHz for 3.75 cm range resolution and tracks up to 64 targets.
sku7.context: SKU-7 separates radio-frequency sensing from digital processing, targeting radar functions for vehicles and other platforms.
sku7.decision: The SiGe front end has no FPGA equivalent; only silicon proves it.

sku8.headline: SKU-8 drives 1280 columns at up to 12 V and flags a frozen image within two frames.
sku8.context: SKU-8 targets rugged displays, combining panel-driving functions with detection of a frozen image.
sku8.decision: Readability and the freeze alert need tests on the target panel.

sku9.headline: SKU-9 switches 16 smart fuses and routes eight CAN-FD buses inside one vehicle zone.
sku9.context: SKU-9 combines network and power-distribution functions within a vehicle zone; the central vehicle computer remains separate.
sku9.decision: Brake-message latency and fuse trips are proven in the vehicle, not on the chip.

sku10.headline: DG32-Max checks signed firmware in 309 ms from reset, on a lockstep RISC-V pair.
sku10.context: DG32-Max targets imported secure microcontrollers and the separate security chip often used to check firmware before it runs.
sku10.decision: RTL is feature-complete as of 1 October 2026; no silicon result yet.

sku11.headline: SKU-11 runs a 4–100 kB battery-health model beside four hardwired protection trips.
sku11.context: SKU-11 brings control, battery-health estimation and authentication together. The cell-measuring and isolation components remain external.
sku11.decision: The measurement partner and field battery data are not yet chosen.

d100.headline: D100 is a 28 nm drone SoC with its own ₹50 Cr round, raised after mature-node revenue.
d100.context: D100 proposes an Indian flight-control and navigation chip, with a failsafe function that remains separate from higher-level computing.
d100.decision: 28 nm development cost and drone qualification set the D100 case.

plan.headline: The business plan, by segment and year.
plan.context: The company model as plan targets: revenue by segment, margins, cash and the P&L, each panel linked to the data behind it. Not results, not audited, not contracted.
plan.decision: Every plan figure links to its data; none is a result, audited or contracted.

portfolio.headline: The SKU portfolio, chip by chip.
portfolio.context: Eleven chips from the October SKU Blueprint: readiness, prototype slot, plan line, revenue ramp, approval time, development and unit cost, each panel linked to the data behind it. Plan targets, not results.
portfolio.decision: Each chip carries its own approval time and revenue ramp.

brief.headline: The investment brief.
brief.context: What tranche 1 buys, how the SKU Blueprint and the September financial model relate, and six buyer questions answered with what is proven and what is a target.
brief.decision: The SKU Blueprint is the chip plan; the ₹10 Cr table is the ask.
